headline: Ireland's data centers consumed 23% of national power in 2025
summary: Data centers in Ireland consumed 7,663 GWh of electricity in 2025, a 10% rise from 2024
details: Data centers in Ireland consumed 7,663 GWh of electricity in 2025, a 10% rise from 2024. This represents a 360% increase from 2015, when data centers' total consumption was just 5% of the national power.
The growth in consumption is even steeper when measured on a quarterly basis. Quarterly data center electricity consumption grew 584% from 291 GWh in Q1 2015 to 1,991 GWh in Q4 2026.

The rise in data center consumption has sparked concerns about their impact on local communities. Critics cite the impact of the immense electricity consumption on residents' bills as one of many concerns.

Ireland has replaced a moratorium on new data center grid connections with a new Large Energy Users (LEU) Connection Policy. Under this policy, developers of new data centers must provide 100% on-site, flexible power generation to meet demand.

Can Ireland's grid handle the growing power demand of data centers?

Data centers in Ireland consumed 7,663 GWh of electricity in 2025, a 10% rise from 2024. This represents a 360% increase from 2015, when data centers' total consumption was just 5% of the national power.

Ireland has replaced a moratorium on new data center grid connections with a new Large Energy Users (LEU) Connection Policy. Under this policy, developers of new data centers must provide 100% on-site, flexible power generation to meet demand.
